solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quickly produce winning blow

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... a piece of work is to turn it out fast
second meaning: the punch that ends a boxing match in victory

explanation.surface: A boxer swiftly lands the punch that wins the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the phrase is a verb for rapid production; as one word, it is the decisive punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock out a job is an idiom for doing it hastily, and a knockout is the boxing blow that wins outright.

clue.text: Knight, a bit dodgy, giving off bad smell

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for an adjective

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
iffy is informal for doubtful or suspect

explanation.surface: A shady knight who also happens to stink.
explanation.walkthrough: NIFFY is British slang: a niff is a whiff or bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Niffy is informal British for smelly, from niff, a slang word for an unpleasant odour.

clue.text: New king had — to be this?

definitions.text: New king had — to be this?

blocks.note: CR, Carolus Rex, is the royal cipher of Charles III, a recent king
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A newly acceded monarch had to undergo a ceremony to become this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a new king must be so treated at his coronation. The dash only adds pause for the wry question.
explanation.definitionFit: A new monarch is formally installed at a coronation, when the regalia is set on his head.

clue.text: Strange old large cup

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: An antique oversized drinking cup looks peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup' suggests a drinking vessel, but here it is a bra size.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and strange are synonyms meaning unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Being drunk, note, is a tricky situation

blocks.note: tight is informal for drunk
to note something is to notice or spot it

explanation.surface: A warning that getting drunk lands you in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a musical note giving one or two letters, but it is the verb meaning observe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight spot is an idiom for an awkward predicament from which escape is hard.

clue.text: Select the best tool

blocks.note: first meaning: to choose, and also the noun for the choicest of a group
second meaning: a pointed implement for breaking hard ground

explanation.surface: Advice to choose the finest implement for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue arguably packs three senses: select, the best, and tool; any two of them confirm the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pick means to choose, names the finest of a group, and is the pointed implement used for breaking rock.

clue.text: Less colourful pair drinking beer

indicators.note: whoever is drinking takes something inside them, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Two people drinking beer look washed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Paler is the comparative of pale, meaning lighter or with less colour.

clue.text: Place in sequence for a Charlie

indicators.note: the word in places the preceding item inside the one that follows

blocks.note: a chain is a series or sequence
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange items in order for someone named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place in sequence' reads as one verb phrase meaning arrange, but it splits into an abbreviation going inside a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the famous silent-film comedian, so he is one example of a person called Charlie.

clue.text: Be able to buy a fine car

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Having enough money to purchase a nice car.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have the means to pay for it.

clue.text: County girl with a baby at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only of the word it follows

blocks.note: gal is informal for girl
W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
the final letter of baby

explanation.surface: A young woman from a particular county who has finally had a child.
explanation.walkthrough: GALWAY is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, on its Atlantic coast.

clue.text: One on the board at church: not her, we're told

definitions.text: One on the board at church

indicators.note: being told something is hearing it spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the male pronoun as opposed to the female one

explanation.surface: Someone posted on a church noticeboard, said to be a man rather than a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Churches display the numbers of the songs to be sung on a hymn board.
explanation.definitionFit: Each number on a church hymn board identifies a religious song in the hymnal for the congregation to sing.

clue.text: Apparently last, as it turns out

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: coming behind everyone else would make you seem to be last
second meaning: in the end, contrary to what was expected

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the phrase; the second is its ordinary idiomatic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom signals an outcome contrary to expectation, while its literal sense, behind everybody, would place one last.

clue.text: Fairly regularly holding the helm for gunners

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the preceding word is taken
to hold something is to grip it within, so the selected letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of fairly
the tiller is the bar that steers a boat

explanation.surface: Taking turns fairly to steer, on behalf of the gun crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly regularly' sounds like an adverb phrase meaning quite often, but 'regularly' picks every other letter of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The artillery is the branch of an army that operates large guns, so its soldiers are gunners.

clue.text: It's fitting in the bathroom to offer extra time

blocks.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
ET is the abbreviation for extra time in sport

explanation.surface: A remark that the bathroom is an appropriate place to suggest overtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' reads as appropriate, but it is the noun: a fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin for washing, plumbed in as a fixture in some bathrooms.

clue.text: Republican slogan maybe is mad

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: a call to exclude the monarch, as an anti-royalist might shout
second meaning: British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an anti-monarchist slogan as crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BAR KING, the answer becomes a slogan to ban the monarch; in Britain a republican is someone who wants to abolish the monarchy, not a US party member.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, from barking mad, is British slang for completely insane.

clue.text: Detective's clothes are so simple

blocks.note: first meaning: an undercover officer works in ... clothes rather than uniform
second meaning: unadorned and straightforward

explanation.surface: An observation that a detective dresses without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unadorned or simple, and plain-clothes police wear ordinary dress instead of uniform.

clue.text: Put into place a quiet fielding position

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket captain stations a silent fielder in a position.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielding position near the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to install them in a post or office.

clue.text: A couple allowed a bit of bling

blocks.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Two people were permitted some flashy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bling is showy jewellery, and a bracelet is an ornamental band worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Long to see river in grotto

indicators.note: in places the first-named item inside the second, as a stream runs inside a cavern

blocks.note: a grotto is a small cave
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Yearning to view an underground stream in a grotto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about size, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to crave it both mean to desire it intensely.

clue.text: Pet sent back small drink

indicators.note: something sent back travels the opposite way, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to sup is to drink, and a sup is a sip

explanation.surface: An animal refused a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' looks like a diner returning a drink, but it turns the following letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is an affectionate name for a cat, the archetypal household pet.

clue.text: Reportedly remained sober

indicators.note: a report is spoken word, so the answer only sounds like the word in the clue

blocks.note: past tense of stay, meaning remained

explanation.surface: Word is that someone stayed off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober' suggests not drunk, but here it means serious and restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid and sober both describe a manner that is serious, respectable and unadventurous.

clue.text: I run into head buccaneer

indicators.note: running into something puts you inside it, so the first two pieces go within the last

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the head
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone collides headlong with a sea robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a sea robber of the Caribbean, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: In cold capital cross the most exciting part

indicators.note: the opening In says the city goes inside the letters for the chilly and angry words around it

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Somewhere chilly, a city's angry finale.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital city sits inside the pair of letters from cold and cross, which bracket it.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the peak of a story or event, the point of greatest intensity.

clue.text: Firm line shows way through mountains

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A company's steady policy points a route over the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a pass or saddle between two mountain peaks, the lowest route across a ridge.

clue.text: Plagued — by a piece of it?

definitions.text: Plagued — by a piece of it?

indicators.note: a piece of something is a fragment lying within it, so the answer is a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run inside this word, between its first two letters and its last

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one is afflicted by a bout of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone plagued by a fever, and the illness sits inside the very word for being plagued.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering fits, something to be plagued by.

clue.text: Lute I'd played in the old festive period

indicators.note: a tune played on an instrument is worked through freely, so these letters are rearranged
in puts the rearranged letters inside the archaic article that follows

blocks.note: ye is a mock-archaic spelling of the
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician recalls strumming an old instrument at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: YE as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe' is a pseudo-archaic form of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the traditional name for the Christmas season.
